ghVariablesTranscript.provenance: gh api graphql --verbose output captured for a representative two-element optionInputArgv() call (an id-bearing element 'Todo' immediately followed by an id-less element 'Blocked') against a harmless query op, to pin the bracket-suffix element-boundary behavior (Task 2 step D fact 3) with a live observation rather than prose. Command: gh api graphql -f query='query{ viewer{ login } }' -f 'options[][name]=Todo' -f 'options[][id]=f75ad846' -f 'options[][color]=GREEN' -f "options[][description]=This item hasn't been started" -f 'options[][name]=Blocked' -f 'options[][color]=RED' -f 'options[][description]=' --verbose
ghVariablesTranscript.observation: gh correctly built a two-element array: the first element carries id=f75ad846 (Todo), the second carries no id (Blocked) — confirming the name-first sub-key emission order in optionInputArgv prevents an id from migrating onto the wrong element, exactly as fact 3 in the plan's <action> requires.
